title: The Deceptions of Demons and the Remedy of Anger
english: The demons have judged gentleness to be a good thing; for even Moses was called this, being gentle toward all men. And the holy David expressed that this was the value of God's remembrance: 'Remember, Lord,' he says, 'David, and all his gentleness' (Ps 89:1). But the Savior himself, imitating us, commanded us to become of that gentleness: 'Learn from me,' he says, 'that I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls' (Matt 11:29). And if someone abstains from filth and drink, but stirs up his mind with evil thoughts, he is like a ship sailing the sea and having a demon as a pilot; therefore, one must observe how much power our dog has, and teach him to destroy only the wolves and not to devour the sheep, which indicates all gentleness toward all men.

Of the thoughts, the one of vainglory is most widespread, almost encompassing the whole inhabited world, and opening the doors to all the demons, just like an evil traitor who becomes of a good city. Therefore, he is very humble toward the one withdrawing the mind, filling him with many words and things, and grieving his prayers through which he strives to heal all the wounds of his soul. All the demons, having been defeated, join together in this thought, and again through it they all gain entrance into souls, making the latter things truly worse than the former. And from this thought is born that one of pride, which has unsealed the likeness and cast down the crown of beauty from the heavens to the earth.

But flee from this, and do not linger, so that we do not betray our life to others and leave our life in misery. One flees from this demon by intense prayer and by doing nothing that contributes to the falling glory. When one seizes a little of the apathy of those withdrawing the mind, then, having acquired a horse of vainglory, he immediately gallops through the cities, carrying unmeasured praise of glory, by which, according to the economy, the spirit of fornication met him, and having shut him into one of the harlots, it teaches him not to leave the bed before perfect health, nor the unruly of the...

However, we must imitate [the wise], for those who still carry the remnants of weakness within themselves, expose themselves to paths and untimely baths, and fall into diseases resulting from turning back. Therefore, sitting [still], let us rather attend to ourselves, since, while we make progress in virtue, we become slow to move against evil, but being renewed in knowledge, we receive a multitude of various contemplations, and being lifted up again, we will more clearly behold the light of our Savior through prayer.

CHAPTER 1. I cannot write all the evils of the demons, and I am ashamed to leave out their wicked crafts, fearing for the simpler ones who will receive them. But besides the spirit of fornication, listen to [the spirit of] cunning. When someone acquires apathy in the part of desire, and the shameful thoughts become merely subconscious, he [the demon] introduces men and women playing with one another, and of shameful things and forms, making the one who withdraws a spectator. But this temptation is not of those who persist; for intense prayer, and the strictest diet with wakefulness, and the exercise of spiritual contemplations, like a cloud, drive him dry. And there is [a time] when he even touches the flesh, purging them toward irrational burning, and this wicked one devises a myriad of other devices, which are not necessary to publish or to hand over in writing. It also contributes greatly to the thoughts and a heat of passion moved against the demon, which he most fears, being disturbed and corrupted by the thoughts; and this is that: 'Be angry, and sin not' (Ephesians 4:26). This is a useful medicine administered to the soul in such temptations. And the one who [uses] anger imitates this demon, and he deceives, and he [makes] some of those born, or friends, or relatives, or household members, being insulted and struck by unworthy ones, and he stirs up the passion of the one withdrawing, so that he might utter something evil, or do something toward those who seem, in thought, to be [enemies] to whom it is not necessary to attend, and he quickly snatches the mind away from such idols, so that, not lingering in them, he might become [distracted] at the time of prayer, like a bellows smoking. By these temptations, the angry [ones]...

title: The Sword of Discernment and the Deception of Gold
english: They fall into it, especially those easily ignited by the passions, which are far from pure prayer and the knowledge of our Savior Jesus Christ.

Chapter 17. The Lord handed over the thoughts of this age to the human, the good shepherd, just like some sheep; for he says he has given the age into his heart, yoking to him a spirit and a desire for help, so that through the spirit he might flee the thoughts of wolves, and through desire he might care for the sheep, being often struck by rains and winds. He also gave to him a law, so that he might shepherd the sheep, and a place of pasture, and water of refreshment, and a psaltery, and a lyre, and a rod, and a staff, so that from this flock he might both be fed, and clothe himself, and gather mountain grass. For who, he says, shepherds a flock and does not eat from the milk of the flock? Therefore, the one withdrawing must guard by night and by day this little flock, lest it become beast-like through thoughts, or fall into robbers; but if such a thing should happen by chance, to snatch it immediately from the mouth of the lion or the bear. And the thought concerning the brother becomes beast-like if the one in us shepherds with hatred, and the thought concerning the woman, if it turns toward us with shameful desire, and the thought of silver and of gold, if it is enticed by greed. And the thoughts of holy gifts, if they were to be grazed by intellect with vainglory; and regarding other thoughts, it will happen likewise, being stolen by the passions.

Chapter 18. It is necessary not only to keep these things in the day, but also to guard by staying awake at night. For it happens that through appearing shameful or evil, one might lose his own; and this is what is said by the holy Jacob: 'Did I not have a sheep that became beast-like? I was tearing away from myself thefts of the day and thefts of the night, and I became joined to the burning of the day and the frost of the night, and sleep stood away from my eyes.' If any weariness or listlessness should come to us, let us run back a little to the rock of knowledge, let us commune with the psaltery, striking the strings of knowledge through virtues, and let us graze...

Again, [the sheep are] under Mount Sinai, so that the God of our fathers may call us out of the bush, and grant us the words of the signs and the wonders. Christ raises up the rational nature having been killed by malice through the contemplation of all the ages; and his Father raises up this dying soul, the death of Christ, through the knowledge of himself.

And this is what is said by Paul: 'If we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him' (Rom 6:4). When the mind, having stripped off the old man, puts on the one from grace, then it will see its own state at a time of prayer, appearing similar in sapphire or heavenly color, which Scripture also names a place of God, having been seen by the elders under Mount Sinai. Chapter 19.

When one of the enemies strikes you by trespassing, and you wish to turn his sword, according to what is written (Ps 38:2), do thus to his heart, as we say. Analyze for yourself the thought cast against you by him, whatever it may be, and from how many things it was composed, and what this is most of all that afflicts the mind.

But what I say is this: Let the thought of love of money be sent by him; analyze this for the mind receiving it, and into the concept of gold, and into the gold itself, and into the passion of love of money; and furthermore ask, which of these is sin, whether the mind, and how? It is the image of God. But the concept of gold? And what could anyone with a mind say about this? But is the gold itself sin? And for whose sake has it become [so]? It follows, therefore, that it is neither a thing subsisting in essence, nor a concept of a thing, nor again an incorporeal mind, but a certain misanthropic pleasure, being produced from the will and being used badly, forcing the mind—which is a creation of God—into [this], which the law of God is believed to circumcise. And while you are investigating these things, the thought will be destroyed by being analyzed into its own contemplation, and the demon will flee from you, your intellect being lifted to a height by this knowledge. title: The Deception of Demons and the Flight of Thoughts
english: Seek the insight of your pastoral staff. How is it that angels and demons exist alongside our world, while we do not exist alongside theirs? For we can no longer join angels to God, nor do we intend to make more unclean demons. And how was the Morning Star, rising early in the earth, cast down, regarding the sea as a refuge and Tartarus of the abyss as a prisoner, while he boils the abyss like bronze, disturbing all through his malice and desiring to rule all? The insight of these things utterly terrifies the demon and makes him flee from all his intrusion. But these things happen only to those purified in solitude, seeing how the words of events unfold. The unclean do not know the insight of these things, nor would they hear them even if they learned from others, due to much dust and noise caused by passions during war. For it is necessary to somewhat quiet the intrusion of the foreigners, so that only Goliath meets our David. Likewise, we shall use this division and this kind of war against all unclean thoughts.

Chapter 40. Regarding unclean demons: some test man as a man, while others disturb man as an irrational animal; the former, casting themselves alongside, implant in us thoughts of vainglory, or pride, or envy, or accusation, which touch nothing of the irrational; the latter, approaching, stir up anger or desire according to nature. For these passions are common to us and to irrational animals, covered by the rational nature. Therefore the Holy Spirit also says, regarding those falling into human thoughts: 'I said: You are gods, and all are sons of the Most High; yet as men you die, and as one of the rulers you fall' (Psalm 82:6). And regarding those moved irrationally, what does He say? 'Do not become like a horse or a mule, which have no understanding, to pull their jaws with bit and bridle, which are not near to you' (Psalm 32:9). And the soul that sins, this one dies. It is evident that men, dying as men, will be buried by men...

And they die like irrational animals, namely, being fallen, they shall be eaten by vultures or crows, whose young ones either call upon the Lord, or are nourished in blood. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

Chapter 22. When some of the impure thoughts are quickly driven away, let us seek the cause from where this has happened; whether because of the scarcity of the matter, it being difficult to find the material, or because of the apathy approaching us, the enemies were not able against us? For example, if one of those retreating is suggested by a demon to believe in the spiritual governance of the first city, this one is evident that he will not delay, imagining this thought, and the cause becomes known from the things said; but if it happens of any city, and by chance, and is similarly thought, this one is blessed with apathy. Similarly, regarding the other thoughts, such a method will be found when being examined. These things are necessary to know for our readiness and power, so that we may see whether we have passed the Jordan (Joshua 3) and are near the city of the Phoenicians, or are still traveling in the wilderness and are being struck by foreigners.

For the demon appears to me very diverse in his love of money, and resourceful for deception, who, having often been constricted by the extremity of renunciation, immediately pretends to be a steward and a lover of the poor, and receives guests more sincerely than those not yet present, and sends service to others who are lacking, and visits the city prisons, and redeems those being sold as slaves, and clings to rich women, and shows those who ought to fare well how to do so, and again admonishes others to dismiss a heavy purse having possessed, and thus, having deceived the soul little by little, he subjects it to the thought of money itself, and delivers it to the demon of vainglory.
